name: Motorcycle
description: Any vehicle with a seat or saddle for the rider, designed to travel on no more than three wheels. Alaska draws the line below it, the motor-driven cycle, only by engine displacement (50 cc or less), with no power or speed equivalent for an electric motor, so a road-going electric motorcycle is registered and licensed as a motorcycle. Defined by Alaska Statutes §28.90.990(a)(21); no e-bike or e-moto bill was enacted in 2025 or 2026.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle for the rider, and no more than three wheels in contact with the ground
No power, speed or pedal limits: the statutes split motorcycles from motor-driven cycles only by a 50 cc engine displacement
Riders need a driver's license with an M1 motorcycle license, from age 16, after a written motorcycle knowledge test, a road test and a vision test
A rider under 18 needs parental consent and must hold an instruction permit for at least 6 months first
A Motorcycle Safety Foundation course certificate can replace the road test
An instruction permit holder must be supervised by a rider at least 21 who has held a license for that class for at least a year
Riders under 18, instruction permit holders and all passengers must wear a helmet; a licensed rider 18 or older needn't
Registered with the DMV to ride on a highway or public parking area, for $60 every two years, and must carry liability insurance
Registration and insurance aren't required in communities off the road system with low traffic, or when ridden only on private property
The rider sits astride the permanent seat facing forward with both hands on the handlebars, and carries a passenger only on a seat built for one
Entitled to a full traffic lane, but may not pass in the same lane or ride between lanes of traffic
